title: Reference data seeding on tenant creation from global template
objective: Creating a tenant auto-populates every configurable reference list from the current global default template inside the creation transaction, plus a default tenant_settings row; template edits affect future tenants only (spec FR-08, PRD 6.3/6.4).
scope: TenantReferenceSeeder invoked by the ITenantProvisioningHook from T-006
Global default template content seeded with the PRD 6.3 value sets (startup seeder, idempotent)
Default tenant_settings row creation (works with T-010 columns; coordinate if T-010 not yet merged — settings row creation may land there instead, decided by whichever merges second)
implementation_details: Infrastructure/Provisioning/TenantReferenceSeeder.cs implements ITenantProvisioningHook: copies default_reference_items -> reference_items for the new tenant preserving name, order, flags, reporting_category, canonical_key, is_terminal; resolves cover-type -> product-line linkage via default_product_line_key mapping to the newly created tenant product-line ids; single transaction with tenant insert

Infrastructure/Provisioning/DefaultTemplateSeeder.cs (IHostedService, idempotent by (list_type,name)): loads PRD 6.3 defaults — request channels (9 incl. broker-channel flags on Broker email, Portal), product lines (12), party types (8), industries (11), party segments (8), regions (9 Botswana), lead statuses (11 canonical with categories and terminal flags per PRD 6.3 table), quote statuses (7), lost reasons (14 per Appendix C, 'Other' flagged requires-comment via canonical_key 'other'), broker types (4); content defined in a single C# data file DefaultReferenceData.cs
CreateTenant handler (T-006) already calls hooks; register seeder in DI; on failure the whole tenant creation rolls back
Audit entry 'tenant.reference_seeded' with counts per list

findings.description: DefaultTemplateSeeder idempotency is only implicitly proven. The seeder is idempotent by (list_type,name) via an existing-keys HashSet and is exercised because all 7 tests call EnsureDefaultTemplateSeededAsync (running StartAsync repeatedly against a shared default_reference_items table), so duplication would trip the unique constraint or inflate seeded counts. But there is no dedicated idempotency assertion.
findings.recommendation: Add one explicit test that calls StartAsync twice and asserts default_reference_items row count is unchanged and equals DefaultReferenceData.All.Count after the second run. Non-blocking.

findings.description: cover_type is seeded with zero default rows. PRD 6.3 defines no cover-type defaults (PRD 27.3 defers them to client discovery), so seeding 'the PRD 6.3 defaults' correctly yields an empty set and inventing values would violate CLAUDE.md's no-silent-gap-filling rule. Evaluator position: acceptable, not a defect. The cover-type->product-line linkage mechanism is implemented and tested via an ad hoc template row (CreateTenant_ShouldLinkCoverTypesToTenantProductLines).
findings.recommendation: Confirm with product that empty cover_type defaults at pilot is intended. No code change required.

findings.description: Quote-status reporting categories / terminal flags were inferred, not tabulated in PRD 6.3. FR-20 requires every status to map to a reporting category and the DB check constraint forbids null/unknown categories, so a mapping is structurally mandatory; the chosen mapping reuses the six spec-defined reporting categories (Open/Quoted/Won/Lost/Expired/Withdrawn) and the same terminal set as lead statuses (Won/Lost/Expired/Withdrawn). Evaluator position: acceptable documented assumption; quote workflow (T-020) not yet built so risk is low.
findings.recommendation: Have product ratify the quote-status category/terminal mapping when T-020 lands. No change required now.
